Subject: EZPay onboarding & invoice submission format question

Hi Karthik / Monica,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As we start onboarding EZPay as a payment reconciliation vendor, our AP team has two technical questions that will determine whether we send invoices via your portal or by email:

1) Do you accept an XML invoice (UBL or cXML) with discrete line items and PO references, or do you require a human-readable PDF?

2) If we email invoices, what fields are mandatory on the PDF header to ensure automatic ingestion (PO number location, vendor remit address, tax id)?

I've attached a sample 3-line invoice and our completed onboarding form to help. We can adapt either format but want to minimize manual touch.

Attachments: [EZPay_InvoiceSample_3line.pdf (PDF, 95 KB)], [EZPay_OnboardingForm_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 48 KB)]

Appreciate any guidance — we want to avoid exceptions on day one.

Subject: Re: EZPay onboarding & invoice submission format question

Hi Sanjay — nice to meet you over email. Quick answers up front, followed by operational notes below.

Short answer: both can work. We prefer structured XML for straight-through processing, but our portal and email ingestion both support automated mapping if the PDF contains the required fields in predictable locations.

Required fields for reliable email->ingest (PDF):
- PO number (exact string PO#) in the top-right or a dedicated header row
- Invoice number and invoice date
- Line-item rows with description, quantity, unit price, and line total (if possible)
- Vendor legal name & tax ID (bottom or header)
- Remit-to address or remit email

Portal advantages: deterministic field extraction, SFTP/XML pickup, and immediate validation errors (rejects with reason). Email advantages: easier for smaller vendors and no portal account setup; higher chance of exceptions for multi-line invoices.

Operational notes / exceptions we should align on:
- If you send XML (UBL/cXML), include PO reference in the <OrderRef> or equivalent; we map it automatically to the PO.
- If you email PDFs, include a machine-readable PO (human-visible PO# + optional barcode) — that reduces manual review.
- For mixed-line formatting (merged descriptions, long text blocks), mark the invoice with an attachment label: "line-delimited" or "single-line-summary" so Ops knows which parser to apply.

Next steps: I can share our AP ingestion schema and an example XML. Monica, can you confirm the SFTP hostname and onboarding SLA (turnaround for first validation)?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk through the sample.

— Karthik Iyer
Head of Procurement, Redwood Inference

2) PDF header placement: our PDF generator is templated and puts PO on the left under vendor info by default. Would that prevent auto-ingest? If so, we can move it to the top-right but prefer to avoid a template sprint if unnecessary.

We tried sending the sample PDF in this thread (same file name), and received a bounce from a validation bot internally — just FYI that small format tweaks trigger rejections during testing.

Attachments: [EZPay_InvoiceSample_3line.pdf]

Hi Priya / Sanjay — thanks for the quick turnaround. Summary and next steps below: 

Summary:
- OrderRef in UBL 2.1 is sufficient for PO mapping.
- For PDFs, PO should be easily regexable (we recommend top-right to avoid template variance, but top-left under vendor info is acceptable if it is always prefixed with "PO#").
- We will share a one-page "ingestion spec" (example XML + required regex patterns) and a short test harness URL for you to upload two sample invoices (one PDF, one XML).

Next steps / owners:
- Karthik: share ingestion spec (by EOD 7/21) — ACTION: share sample XML and list of required element names (done).
- Monica: send SFTP/Sandbox details and a short troubleshooting playbook (ACTION: send by 7/22).
- EZPay (Priya): send back one PDF with PO clearly labeled (PO#123456) and one UBL XML sample to the sandbox by 7/27 so we can validate.

Marissa — looping you in for billing setup once validation passes (PO stamping and vendor code). We'll treat the first two invoices as onboarding tests and not count them toward early payment terms.

I'll attach the ingestion spec and sandbox link in a follow-up. Thanks all.

Best,
Monica Patel
Vendor Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference
